The thickness of your safe's steel is the single most important factor in whether it will resist a break-in. We don't hide this number — we lead with it.
American A36-Grade 50 steel — every sheet sourced from domestic mills
Why steel thickness matters more than anything else

14-gauge steel is .075 inches thick — thinner than two stacked nickels. A motivated burglar with a reciprocating saw can cut through it in minutes. Sturdy Safe bodies start at .22 inches: nearly three times thicker. Our doors use 3/8" (.375") plate steel. These aren't marketing numbers. You can verify them with a $10 caliper.

Construction Method

One sheet of steel.
Twelve bends. No weak seams.

Sturdy safes are formed from a single sheet of steel bent twelve times. This eliminates vertical seams and splicing at the door seat — the two weakest points on a conventional safe. The twelve bends create a Quadra-Formed Door Seat: two additional bends at the door opening that add rigidity and give locking bolts a stronger surface to grab.

Weld Quality

Every seam is hot welded

Skip welds (competitors)

Gaps between welds create flex points where a pry bar can find purchase or heat can penetrate during a fire.

Continuous hot welds (Sturdy)

Unbroken weld bead along every seam. No gaps, no flex, no penetration points. The weld is as strong as the surrounding steel.

settings.text: Every sheet of steel in a Sturdy Safe is sourced from American mills — A36 to Grade 50. We don't import steel and call the safe "American made." The steel is American. The fabrication is in Fresno. The people who build your safe are the same people who answer your phone call.
